description: Reusable proof prerequisites for proof-carrying Type-4 frontier packets. Target packets cite these fact_id values; packet-local models may add only packet-specific current status.

evidence_requirement_vocabulary.focused-executable: A focused positive or hard-negative expectation must exercise the fact boundary.
evidence_requirement_vocabulary.formal-or-mechanized: A formal proof, proof obligation, or machine-checked model must justify the rewrite precondition.
evidence_requirement_vocabulary.source-evidence: The source program must expose evidence for the fact; names alone are not enough.

accepted_evidence: ordered integer literal bounds
asserted Guard(BoundOrder) evidence on a dominating exiting inverse guard, for example if hi < lo then raise/return/throw before the clamp
asserted Guard(BoundOrder) evidence on a positive branch guard, for example if lo <= hi then evaluate the clamp and the other branch exits
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a real clamp pair by itself; the paired members must also satisfy numeric-clamp.integer-domain.
implementation_guidance: Represent only dominating exiting inverse guards and positive branch guards as bound-order evidence.
Reject parameter naming, non-exiting checks, swapped bounds, and wrong min/max nesting.
rejected_evidence: parameter names such as lower/upper or minimum/maximum
non-exiting guard expressions
swapped bounds or wrong min/max nesting
facts.summary: The lower bound must be proven <= the upper bound before min(max(x, lo), hi), max(min(x, hi), lo), ternary clamp, and library clamp forms can share a Clamp value.
facts.title: Clamp bound order

accepted_evidence: integer literals
asserted integer parameter/domain evidence on each clamp operand
language/type evidence that excludes float, NaN, and non-total-order behavior
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a real clamp pair by itself; the paired members must also satisfy numeric-clamp.bound-order.
implementation_guidance: Gate clamp canonicalization to integer-domain operands.
Keep language domains that can include floats or NaN outside exact clamp admission.
rejected_evidence: Python dynamic numeric parameters without integer-domain evidence
TypeScript/JavaScript number domains
Go cmp.Ordered or other generic ordered domains that can include floats
facts.summary: Clamp canonicalization is restricted to integer-domain operands so float/NaN-sensitive min/max and comparison-chain forms stay closed.
facts.title: Clamp integer domain

accepted_evidence: comparison predicates whose results are booleans
the same element variable and the same literal/value coordinates on both sides
a boolean context where operand values are not observed
language or source evidence that excludes overloaded, value-returning, or effectful boolean operands
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a quantifier/loop convergence by itself; source identity, purity, counterexample-loop, and vacuous-truth facts are separate requirements.
implementation_guidance: Normalize De Morgan only when operands are proven boolean values.
Reject value-returning boolean contexts, overloaded comparison semantics, and predicate calls unless separate effect/purity evidence exists.
Attach new language surfaces by emitting boolean-operand evidence, not by adding language-specific detector branches.
rejected_evidence: value-returning and/or operands whose value, not only truthiness, is observed
overloaded comparison or predicate calls with effects
changed predicates such as x != 0 or x != 1
facts.summary: A De Morgan rewrite may be used only when both sides operate on proven boolean operands, not on language-specific value-returning boolean expressions.
facts.title: De Morgan over proven boolean operands

accepted_evidence: a universal quantifier/all/every surface over a single element predicate
an explicit loop whose only counterexample branch returns literal false
matching predicate coordinates between the quantifier and the loop counterexample
short-circuit order that stops at the first counterexample
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a loop/quantifier convergence by itself; vacuous truth, source identity, predicate purity, and any boolean rewrite facts remain separate.
implementation_guidance: Model only loops where the counterexample branch is the sole early false exit.
Keep extra loop control, observed loop effects, and unsupported body shapes closed until separate evidence exists.
Pair this fact with quantifier.vacuous-truth before admitting an all/every-style surface.
rejected_evidence: counterexample branches that return non-false payloads
loop bodies with extra observed effects, break, continue, else effects, or unsupported control
predicate-coordinate changes between the quantifier and the loop
facts.summary: A universal quantifier can match an early-return loop only when the loop is a pure counterexample scan that returns false at the first not-P element.
facts.title: Universal quantifier as counterexample loop

accepted_evidence: the quantifier surface returns true for an empty input
the explicit loop falls through to literal true after exhausting the same input
no loop else block, final payload, or post-loop effect changes the empty-input result
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a quantifier/loop convergence by itself; it only closes the empty-input boundary for a separately proven counterexample loop.
implementation_guidance: Treat empty-input behavior as a first-class proof fact, not as a side effect of loop-shape matching.
Keep loops that return false or a payload after exhaustion outside all/every admission.
Require this fact whenever a universal quantifier surface is matched to an explicit loop.
rejected_evidence: fallthrough returns false or a non-boolean payload
post-loop code changes the empty-input result
collection APIs with non-vacuous empty behavior
facts.summary: Universal quantifier rewrites must preserve the empty-input result: no counterexamples means true.
facts.title: Universal quantifier vacuous truth

accepted_evidence: the quantifier and explicit loop consume the same local iterable binding or receiver place
no reassignment or mutation changes the source between the two forms
the quantifier element and loop element refer to the same traversal coordinate
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a quantifier/loop convergence by itself; it only rules out different receivers, iterators, or traversal sources.
implementation_guidance: Require same-source provenance for the quantifier and loop traversal.
Reject different iterable bindings, mutated receivers, and derived iterables whose order/cardinality relation is not proven.
Let each frontend emit receiver/place evidence for its language surface.
rejected_evidence: different iterable bindings or receiver places
receiver or iterator mutation during traversal
derived iterables whose cardinality/order relationship is not proven
facts.summary: The quantifier and explicit loop must traverse the same source in the same order before their predicates can be compared.
facts.title: Iteration same-source identity

accepted_evidence: local comparisons over the loop or quantifier element and literals
no calls, assignments, yields, awaits, mutations, or logging inside the predicate or loop body
no observed state before the early return or inside the quantifier predicate
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a quantifier/loop convergence by itself; it only permits comparing short-circuit boundaries after predicate effects are closed.
implementation_guidance: Treat helper calls, mutation, logging, yield, await, and assignment as closed unless separate purity/effect evidence exists.
Keep short-circuit timing as behavior-defining when side effects can be observed.
Attach language surfaces through effect evidence producers or admitted purity resolvers.
rejected_evidence: predicate helper calls unless callee purity is proven
observed counters or logging before return
iterator, receiver, or captured-state mutation during traversal
facts.summary: The predicate must be pure enough that quantifier and loop short-circuiting observe the same effects and stop at the same first counterexample.
facts.title: Pure predicate/effect safety

accepted_evidence: callback bodies made only of local value construction, comparisons, field reads, and pure arithmetic over the current element
no logging, mutation, assignment, yield, await, throw, or helper call with unknown effects inside the callback
focused hard negatives that keep observed callback effects behavior-defining
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit HoF convergence by itself; receiver/source identity, callback meaning, and output-channel facts remain separate requirements.
implementation_guidance: Use this for map/filter/filter_map/flat_map callbacks, not just boolean predicates.
Treat helper calls, mutation, logging, yield, await, throw, and assignment as closed without separate effect evidence.
Keep evaluation timing and observed callback effects out of value-only HoF facts.
rejected_evidence: callbacks that print, log, mutate, assign, yield, await, throw, or call unproven helpers
callbacks whose laziness or evaluation timing is observable
receiver or captured-state mutation during callback execution
facts.summary: Higher-order callback rewrites may compare value outputs only after callback effects and evaluation timing are proven unobservable for the admitted surface.
facts.title: Pure callback/effect safety

accepted_evidence: filter_map, compactMap, or equivalent callback forms whose absence branch drops exactly the same elements as the explicit filter predicate
guarded builders that push only on the same drop-condition complement
match, if-let, and and_then-style option forms that expose the same absence condition
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit filter-map convergence by itself; emitted value, source identity, option channel, and callback purity facts remain separate.
implementation_guidance: Treat the drop condition as a first-class coordinate distinct from the emitted value expression.
Reject changed predicates, inverted predicates, extra filters, and post-filter drops unless a separate proof connects them.
Keep explicit filter+map chains and option-producing callbacks connected through this fact, not through API spelling.
rejected_evidence: same emitted value with a changed filter/drop predicate
extra post-filter conditions that can remove emitted values
truthiness checks that decide dropping from the emitted payload instead of the option channel
facts.summary: Filter-map convergence requires proof that both surfaces drop exactly the same source elements before emitted values are compared.
facts.title: Filter-map drop-condition coordinate

accepted_evidence: the Some/Just/present branch emits the same value coordinate as the explicit map expression
guarded builders push the same value expression as the option-producing callback emits
literal, parameter, field, or arithmetic coordinates are preserved through lowering
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit filter-map convergence by itself; drop condition, source identity, option channel, and callback purity facts remain separate.
implementation_guidance: Compare emitted values independently from the condition that decides whether a value is emitted.
Reject Some/Just payload changes, derived payloads, and wrong pushed values unless a separate value proof connects them.
Keep wrapped absence payloads as emitted values when the option channel says they are present.
rejected_evidence: same drop condition with a changed emitted value
mapping Option/Maybe values as payloads instead of emitting their inner present values
derived emitted values without a value-equivalence proof
facts.summary: Filter-map convergence requires the present branch, explicit map expression, or guarded push to emit the same value coordinate.
facts.title: Filter-map emitted value coordinate

accepted_evidence: language API evidence that distinguishes the option/nullable absence channel from present payload values
falsey payloads such as 0, false, or empty strings that remain emitted when wrapped as present values
wrapped absence payloads such as Some(None) that remain present values in nested option domains
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit optional-emission convergence by itself; it only closes the absence-vs-payload channel boundary.
implementation_guidance: Model absence by the option/nullable channel, not by payload truthiness.
Preserve falsey present payloads and nested absence payloads as emitted values.
Require API identity evidence for language-specific helpers such as Rust Option, Swift Optional, Kotlin nullable values, or JS nullish protocols.
rejected_evidence: truthy filters that drop falsey present payloads
nullish/defaulting idioms that erase present null payload distinctions
custom option-like helpers without API identity evidence
facts.summary: Optional-emission rewrites may drop only the proven absence channel; falsey and nested present payloads remain behavior-defining values.
facts.title: Option absence channel identity

accepted_evidence: a flat-map, multi-clause comprehension, or nested builder whose output appends every inner element in outer iteration order
source evidence that the same inner collection is traversed for each corresponding outer element
no extra filter, early exit, mutation, or receiver substitution changes the outer/inner traversal coordinates
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit flat-map convergence by itself; flatten depth, emitted value, source identity, and callback purity facts remain separate.
implementation_guidance: Track outer and inner iteration coordinates separately.
Reject changed inner receivers, reordered traversal, dropped outer iterations, and derived inner collections without source evidence.
Use this fact for one-level flat-map and for later flat-map aggregate surfaces.
rejected_evidence: same emitted expression over a different inner collection
receiver mutation or substitution between outer and inner traversal
extra outer or inner filters without separate predicate-coordinate proof
facts.summary: Flat-map convergence requires the same nested traversal order: each outer element exposes the same inner source before emitted values are flattened.
facts.title: Flat-map nested iteration order

accepted_evidence: the inner map, builder push, or yielded value computes the same expression for each matched outer/inner coordinate
literal, parameter, field, or arithmetic coordinates are preserved through comprehension, stream, and callback lowering
focused hard negatives that change the inner emitted value remain split
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit flat-map convergence by itself; traversal order, flatten depth, source identity, and callback purity facts remain separate.
implementation_guidance: Compare emitted values after outer and inner coordinates are matched.
Reject changed inner map expressions, wrong pushed values, and derived values without a value-equivalence proof.
Keep aggregate terminals separate; this fact only describes the flattened element stream.
rejected_evidence: same nested traversal with a changed yielded or pushed expression
callbacks that emit the outer element instead of the inner mapped value
aggregate results whose terminal operation changes the observed value
facts.summary: Flat-map convergence requires the callback, comprehension, or nested builder to emit the same value for every matched nested iteration coordinate.
facts.title: Flat-map emitted value coordinate

accepted_evidence: flatMap, flat_map, stream flatMap, or multi-clause comprehension semantics that flatten exactly one collection layer
nested builder loops that append inner elements into a single output collection
hard negatives where map-returning-collection or nested-list outputs remain nested
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit flat-map convergence by itself; it only closes the flattened-vs-nested shape boundary for separately proven traversal and value facts.
implementation_guidance: Represent exactly one layer of flattening, not recursive flattening or identity map.
Reject map-returning-collection forms unless a flat-map or join proof supplies this fact.
Reject scalar callback results for APIs whose flat-map contract requires a collection.
rejected_evidence: map returning a nested collection without flattening
recursive or depth-unbounded flattening
scalar callback results under a collection-producing flat-map contract
facts.summary: Flat-map and nested-builder rewrites must prove exactly one collection layer is flattened so nested-list/map shapes stay behavior-defining.
facts.title: One-level flatten depth

accepted_evidence: language standard membership APIs over a proven collection receiver, such as Python in, JS/TS Array.includes or Set.has, Go slices.Contains, Java Collection.contains, Ruby include?/member?, Rust contains, and Swift contains
membership-like higher-order surfaces whose boolean result is proven to be an existence predicate, such as some/findIndex/indexOf/filter-length comparisons or their negated absence forms
type, import, constructor, package, or receiver evidence that separates collection membership from substring, regex, map-key, value, and custom contains semantics
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit membership convergence by itself; element coordinate, collection/source coordinate, and mutation closure remain separate facts.
implementation_guidance: Attach membership semantics only after the receiver domain and API identity are proven.

Reject method-name-only contains/has/include calls, JavaScript in, substring contains, regex contains, raw index/count payloads, loose equality predicates, and shadowed or missing standard-library constructors.
Keep map-key membership on a separate map-key semantic family even when the surface spelling is contains/has.
rejected_evidence: substring, regex, or string receiver contains calls
map-key membership or map-value search without an explicit collection-membership domain
raw indexOf/findIndex/filter length values whose numeric payload is observed
missing imports, shadowed constructors, untyped dynamic has receivers, or custom contains methods
facts.summary: Collection membership surfaces require proven receiver domain and API identity before contains/has/include-shaped calls can be treated as element-in-collection predicates.
facts.title: Collection membership API/domain identity

accepted_evidence: the searched element coordinate is the same local value, parameter, literal, imported value, or lowered expression on both surfaces
membership and negated-membership forms compare the same element coordinate against the collection
focused wrong-element hard negatives remain split
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit membership convergence by itself; receiver/API domain, collection/source coordinate, and mutation closure remain separate facts.
implementation_guidance: Track the searched element independently from the collection source.
Reject value-to-other substitutions even when all collection evidence still matches.
For callback-based membership encodings, bind the callback comparison to the searched element coordinate before canonicalizing.
rejected_evidence: same collection with a changed searched element
callback comparisons against a different parameter or captured value
derived element expressions without a separate value-equivalence proof
facts.summary: Collection membership is a predicate over a specific searched element coordinate; changing that coordinate changes behavior.
facts.title: Collection membership element coordinate

accepted_evidence: static literal collections with the same element set or sequence under the collection kind's equality/order semantics
standard collection factories, module-level bindings, imports, package/static fields, or typed dynamic receivers whose source provenance is proven
focused wrong-collection and provider-provenance hard negatives remain split
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit membership convergence by itself; receiver/API domain, searched element coordinate, and mutation closure remain separate facts.
implementation_guidance: Preserve the collection kind/source coordinate separately from the searched element.
Use import, package, static-field, and constructor identity evidence for cross-file or factory-backed collections.
Reject same-shaped literals or same variable names when provenance, type/domain, or collection contents differ.
rejected_evidence: different literal items or provider exports
same receiver spelling without import/type/source proof
single-argument Java Arrays.asList over an unproven non-array receiver
enum or field-chain elements whose value identity is not strict-safe
facts.summary: Collection membership requires the same proven collection source or dynamic receiver coordinate, including collection-kind and constructor/import provenance.
facts.title: Collection membership collection/source coordinate

accepted_evidence: no writes, adds, appends, inserts, fills, deletes, or mutating method calls can affect the collection receiver before the membership check
imported or module-level collections are immutable, frozen, or treated as stable literal provenance
provider and importer modules both preserve the collection state before membership
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit membership convergence by itself; it only closes mutation and stale-receiver boundaries for separately proven membership surfaces.
implementation_guidance: Reject receiver mutation after construction/import and before membership.
Treat provider-side and importer-side mutations as separate stale-provenance blockers.
Keep helper calls that may mutate the receiver outside strict membership proof unless a separate effect/immutability proof exists.
rejected_evidence: append/add/insert/push/fill/copyWithin or assignment to the collection before membership
provider module mutates an exported collection after initialization
importer mutates an imported collection before reading membership
helper calls that may mutate the collection receiver
facts.summary: Collection membership over constructed, imported, or typed receivers requires a stable receiver state; mutation changes the membership predicate.
facts.title: Collection membership mutation closure

accepted_evidence: length, size, truthiness, or named-empty surfaces read the same local receiver place
the empty and non-empty predicates refer to the same parameter, local binding, field, or imported receiver coordinate
focused wrong-receiver hard negatives remain split
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit empty-check convergence by itself; collection domain/kind, predicate direction, and mutation closure remain separate facts.
implementation_guidance: Track the receiver coordinate independently from the empty/non-empty predicate spelling.
Reject same-shaped predicates over a different parameter, field, or derived receiver unless a separate alias/source fact proves identity.
For method and property surfaces, attach the fact to the receiver place rather than to the method name.
rejected_evidence: length or named-empty checks over a different receiver
derived receivers such as filtered, sliced, or copied collections without a source-preservation fact
same variable names across files without import, type, or binding evidence
facts.summary: Collection empty-check predicates compare the state of a specific receiver coordinate; changing that receiver changes behavior.
facts.title: Collection empty-check receiver coordinate

accepted_evidence: type, import, constructor, package, or receiver evidence proves the receiver is the same collection domain and kind
array, list, set, map, queue, and sequence emptiness are matched only when the kind-specific empty state is behavior-compatible
real and focused hard negatives keep collection, array, map, and string empty domains split without domain proof
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit empty-check convergence by itself; receiver coordinate, predicate direction, and mutation closure remain separate facts.
implementation_guidance: Require a proven collection-domain and kind before folding length, size, named-empty, or truthiness surfaces.
Keep string emptiness, Java array length, map-key domain, custom isEmpty-like APIs, and untyped receivers closed without explicit domain evidence.
Use language frontends and library contracts to emit domain/kind evidence instead of relying on spelling alone.
rejected_evidence: string or substring emptiness folded into collection emptiness by name
array length, map emptiness, and collection emptiness merged without kind compatibility proof
custom empty/isEmpty methods or shadowed standard-library APIs without API identity
facts.summary: Empty-check convergence requires a compatible collection domain and kind, so string, array, map, and custom empty surfaces stay distinct unless explicitly proven.
facts.title: Collection empty-check domain and kind identity

accepted_evidence: length or size equals zero, named empty predicates, and collection truthiness surfaces are normalized to the empty direction only when the boolean result is observed
length or size not-equals zero, negated named empty predicates, and supported non-empty truthiness surfaces are normalized to the non-empty direction
focused threshold and direction hard negatives remain split
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit empty-check convergence by itself; receiver coordinate, domain/kind identity, and mutation closure remain separate facts.
implementation_guidance: Represent empty and non-empty as opposite boolean directions over the same receiver proof.
Reject one-length, greater-than-one, raw length payload, and compound arithmetic forms unless a separate cardinality proof admits them.
For truthiness, require language-specific collection-domain evidence and a boolean context so payload values are not observed.
rejected_evidence: len(x) == 1, len(x) > 1, or other cardinality thresholds
raw length/size numeric payloads whose value is observed
truthiness over unproven or value-returning domains
facts.summary: Length-zero, named-empty, truthiness, and their negations must preserve the empty versus non-empty boolean direction.
facts.title: Collection empty/non-empty predicate direction

accepted_evidence: no writes, pushes, appends, inserts, clears, removals, deletes, or mutating method calls can affect the receiver before the empty check
imported or module-level collections are immutable, frozen, or treated as stable literal provenance before the check
focused mutation hard negatives remain split from the original empty predicate
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit empty-check convergence by itself; it only closes mutation and stale-receiver boundaries for separately proven empty-check surfaces.
implementation_guidance: Reject receiver mutation after construction/import and before the empty or non-empty predicate.
Treat provider-side and importer-side collection mutations as stale-provenance blockers.
Keep helper calls that may mutate the receiver outside strict empty-check proof unless a separate effect/immutability proof exists.
rejected_evidence: push/append/add/insert/remove/clear/delete or assignment to the collection before the empty check
provider module mutates an exported collection after initialization
helper calls that may mutate the collection receiver
facts.summary: Collection empty-checks over constructed, imported, or typed receivers require a stable receiver state; mutation changes the empty/non-empty predicate.
facts.title: Collection empty-check mutation closure

accepted_evidence: sum, reduce, any, all, or equivalent loop terminals with the same initial value or empty-input result
loop accumulators whose seed matches the aggregate terminal identity
focused hard negatives where changed seeds or empty-input behavior remain split
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit aggregate convergence by itself; it only closes seed and empty-input behavior for separately proven source, step, and effect facts.
implementation_guidance: Track aggregate identities such as additive 0, any false, all true, and explicit reduce seeds.
Reject selection reductions whose loop seed clamps behavior differently from the terminal API.
Keep terminal APIs that can throw on empty input outside this fact unless matching empty-input behavior is proven.
rejected_evidence: wrong additive or multiplicative seed
zero-seeded max/min loops compared with unseeded terminal max/min
early-return loops with a mismatched fallthrough value
facts.summary: Aggregate rewrites must preserve the terminal identity, explicit seed, and empty-input behavior before loop and higher-order reductions may converge.
facts.title: Reduction identity and empty-input behavior

accepted_evidence: the aggregate step combines the accumulator with the same flattened element value
any/all predicates observe the same flattened element coordinate as the explicit early-return loop
focused hard negatives where changed terminal predicates or contribution expressions remain split
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit aggregate convergence by itself; source identity, flattening, identity/empty behavior, and effect facts remain separate.
implementation_guidance: Compare reduction step expressions after the flattened element coordinate is established.
For any/all terminals, compare the terminal predicate independently from upstream filters.
Reject aggregate terminals that observe the outer coordinate, nested row, or a changed predicate without a separate value proof.
rejected_evidence: terminal any/all predicate changed while traversal is unchanged
reduction contribution changed from the flattened emitted value
aggregate over nested rows instead of flattened elements
facts.summary: Aggregate rewrites must preserve the reduction step, terminal predicate, or contribution expression for every proven flattened element coordinate.
facts.title: Reduction step coordinate identity

accepted_evidence: outer and inner filters in a flat-map aggregate guard the same matched traversal coordinates
nested guarded loops and flat-map/filter chains preserve the same guard placement before aggregation
focused hard negatives where outer, inner, or terminal predicates are changed remain split
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit aggregate convergence by itself; it only closes guard placement after nested traversal and terminal step facts are proven.
implementation_guidance: Track whether a predicate guards the outer traversal, inner traversal, or terminal aggregate.
Reject predicates moved across coordinates unless a separate equivalence proof preserves cardinality and short-circuit behavior.
Keep numeric or ordering predicates closed when their domain proof is missing.
rejected_evidence: outer guard changed while inner and terminal expressions remain unchanged
inner guard changed while outer and terminal expressions remain unchanged
terminal predicate substituted for an upstream filter or vice versa
facts.summary: Filtered flat-map aggregate rewrites must preserve whether each guard belongs to the outer traversal, inner traversal, or terminal aggregate coordinate.
facts.title: Flat-map aggregate guard coordinate

accepted_evidence: map get/index lookup paired with an explicit fallback only for absent keys
membership guard plus lookup returning the same fallback for absence
language API evidence that separates absent-key fallback from present key with null/nil/None payload
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit map-default convergence by itself; receiver identity, key/default coordinates, and mutation closure remain separate facts.
implementation_guidance: Model only absence-default APIs or guards whose fallback fires on missing keys.
Keep nullish/truthy defaulting and present-null payload semantics outside this fact.
Require a separate API identity proof for language helpers such as Python get, JS Map.get with has, Java Map.getOrDefault, Rust HashMap lookup, and Swift dictionary default subscripts.
rejected_evidence: nullish coalescing on a map read without absent-key proof
truthy/default idioms that treat present falsey values as absent
custom helper names without API identity evidence

facts.title: Map default absence fallback

accepted_evidence: the compared lookups read from the same local map binding, imported immutable map, or statically proven map literal source
module/export/static field provenance for imported literal maps
no alias changes the receiver between construction/import and lookup
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit map-default convergence by itself; it only proves that both sides query the same map value source.
implementation_guidance: Reuse import/projection evidence for cross-file literal map sources.
Reject same-shaped literals or same variable names that do not share source provenance.
Keep different map receivers split even when key and default literals match.
rejected_evidence: different map bindings or imported exports
same-shaped map literals with no shared provenance
receiver aliases whose source cannot be traced

accepted_evidence: the lookup key coordinates are equal on both surfaces
the fallback/default value coordinates are equal on both surfaces
literal, imported, or parameter coordinates are preserved through lowering
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit map-default convergence by itself; it only closes the key/default coordinate boundary.

accepted_evidence: no writes, updates, deletes, or mutating method calls can affect the map receiver before lookup
imported literal maps are immutable or treated as frozen evidence
guard and lookup read the same receiver state

implementation_guidance: Reject receiver mutation between map construction/import and lookup.
Reject guard/read pairs if mutation can happen between the guard and the read.
Treat cross-file imported maps as stable only when import/export evidence proves immutable literal provenance.

guarded lookups with intervening writes

accepted_evidence: comparison predicates whose results are booleans
the same element variable and the same literal/value coordinates on both sides
a boolean context where operand values are not observed

accepted_evidence: local comparisons over the loop variable and literals
no calls, assignments, yields, awaits, or mutations inside the predicate or loop body
no observed state before the early return or inside the all(...) predicate

facts.summary: The predicate must be pure and exact-safe so all(...) short-circuit and the early-return loop observe the same effects and stop at the same first counterexample.
facts.title: Loop/all effect safety

accepted_evidence: all(...) and the explicit loop consume the same local iterable binding
no reassignment or mutation changes the iterable between the two forms
the generator and loop use the same element variable coordinate
facts.detector_admission_implication: Retired compatibility alias; new packets must cite iteration.same-source-identity.
implementation_guidance: Require same local iterable provenance for all(...) and the loop.
Reject forms where all(...) ranges over xs but the loop ranges over ys or over a mutated receiver.
rejected_evidence: different iterable bindings
receiver or iterator mutation during traversal
derived iterables whose cardinality/order relationship is not proven
facts.summary: The generator consumed by all(...) and the explicit loop must traverse the same iterable in the same order.
facts.title: Loop/all iterator identity

accepted_evidence: a single for-loop over the same local iterable
only the counterexample branch returns False
fallthrough return is literal True
empty iterables return True in both forms
facts.detector_admission_implication: Retired compatibility alias; new packets must cite quantifier.universal.counterexample-loop and quantifier.vacuous-truth.
implementation_guidance: Model the explicit loop as universal quantification only when the counterexample branch is the sole early False return and fallthrough returns literal True.
Keep wrong empty-input truth and extra loop control/effects closed.
rejected_evidence: fallthrough returns False or a non-boolean payload
loop body has break, continue, else effects, or extra observed state
the loop consumes a different iterable or mutates the iterable
facts.summary: A Python early-return loop that returns False on the first counterexample and True after exhaustion is equivalent to all(P(x) for x in xs) only with vacuous truth and matching short-circuit behavior.
facts.title: Universal loop short-circuit and vacuous truth

status_vocabulary.admitted-real-pair: The fact is reusable and has current real-pair evidence, but detector admission still depends on every fact required by the packet.
status_vocabulary.modeled-controlled: The fact is implemented or machine-checked for controlled evidence; individual real-corpus members still need source evidence.
status_vocabulary.retired: The fact id is retained only for historical artifacts and should not be cited by new packets.
status_vocabulary.specified-not-modeled: The fact is specified as a reusable prerequisite, but no detector/proof implementation can consume it yet.
